title: Towards Fairness Assessment of Dutch Hate Speech Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual substitution of nationality-related Dutch Social Group Terms (e.g., Dutch, Moroccan, Turk) using LLMs and dictionary-based methods, followed by evaluating hate speech detection consistency via Counterfactual Token Fairness (CTF) and group fairness metrics.
Swapping skin color terminology (e.g., white, black, dark) in text to measure if the BERTje model alters its hate speech classifications based on the counterfactual presence of racial terms.
Replacing gender identity terms (e.g., woman, man, transgender, non-binary) to test for counterfactual fairness and computing Demographic Parity and Equalized Odds.

Generating counterfactual sentences by substituting terms related to sexuality (e.g., homosexual, heterosexual, bisexual) and measuring the Counterfactual Token Fairness (CTF) of the model's toxicity predictions.
Modifying sentences by changing religious group identifiers (e.g., Christian, Muslim, Jewish) to calculate the absolute difference in the model's hate speech probability predictions.
Substituting age-related terms (e.g., older, younger, adult, student) in the text inputs and evaluating if the classification outcomes change unfairly.
Replacing political and ideological descriptors (e.g., Marxist, populist, feminist, liberal) in Dutch phrases and assessing fairness using counterfactual and group fairness metrics.
